## Overview

Some deployments use a main model from ModelScope and a draft model from Hugging Face. The global `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` switch cannot express this combination. This PR adds explicit, per-model Hub selection.

For example, use [GLM-4.7-Flash from ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.7-Flash) with [thoughtworks/GLM-4.7-Flash-Eagle3 from Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/thoughtworks/GLM-4.7-Flash-Eagle3). I could not find a same-ID ModelScope mirror of this draft.

```bash
vllm serve modelscope://ZhipuAI/GLM-4.7-Flash \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"hf://thoughtworks/GLM-4.7-Flash-Eagle3","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## Claims

- Support `hf://owner/model` and `modelscope://owner/model` for the model, tokenizer, and speculative draft model.
- Explicit prefixes override the global Hub setting; bare `owner/model` IDs and local paths retain their existing behavior.
- Resolve explicit sources into local SDK snapshots before normal loading, reusing authentication and caching without cross-Hub fallback.
- Keep ModelScope optional and the shared helper under `transformers_utils`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_model_hub.py \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py -q --tb=short
# 47 passed

VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_model_hub.py \
  -k 'hf_downloader_survives or mixed_sources' -q --tb=short
# 5 passed
```

Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed. A GPU integration test is included but has not been run locally; model evaluation is pending.

## Details

The initial scope is single-node Python execution with `auto`, `hf`, `safetensors`, or `pt` loaders. Explicit model sources download repository snapshots, potentially including multiple weight formats; tokenizer-only sources download metadata without weights.

Cross-repository `auto_map`, separate code revisions, and automatic speculator target inference are outside this initial scope. Unsupported cases fail explicitly and can use pre-downloaded local paths instead. This revision removes the earlier loader-specific changes.

Prior open-PR searches found no direct match for per-model HF/ModelScope selection. AI assistance was used.

---

🔴 Users who add an `hf://` or `modelscope://` prefix now download the whole repo, including weights vLLM never loads. A bare ID only fetches what the loader selects. Unless load_format is dummy, `ignore_patterns` is None, so the snapshot pulls every file. That includes `original/` .pth checkpoints, duplicate .bin/.safetensors copies and every GGUF quant. The metadata-only deny-list at :51 also misses *.h5, *.msgpack and *.onnx. Fix: build an allow-list from the loader's rules for the load format, and apply LoadConfig `ignore_patterns` (default `original/**/*`). For tokenizer and dummy downloads, allow only config, tokenizer and code files.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `vllm serve hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` or `modelscope://...`, which reaches resolve_model_source via EngineArgs.create_model_config (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:943). There, metadata_only is False, so `ignore_patterns` is None (vllm/model_hub.py:50-54), and snapshot_download fetches every file in the repo. On the base branch, DefaultModelLoader downloads only allow_patterns such as ["*.safetensors"] (default_loader.py:186-201). It also honors LoadConfig.ignore_patterns, which defaults to ["original/**/*"] (vllm/config/load.py:102). For Llama-3 repos that adds a second full consolidated .pth copy. For GGUF repos it adds every quantization, and repos that keep both .bin and .safetensors double the download. The local-path loader skips its own filtering download, so nothing removes this cost. `self.ignore_patterns` (arg_utils.py:712) is never passed to resolve_model_source. The tokenizer download (arg_utils.py:960) and the dummy download still pull TF/Flax/ONNX weights (*.h5, *.msgpack, *.onnx), because the deny-list at model_hub.py:51 does not cover them.

**Verification:** vllm/model_hub.py:47-55 sets `"ignore_patterns": ([...] if metadata_only else None)` and passes no allow_patterns, so every file in the repo is downloaded. EngineArgs.create_model_config calls `resolve_source(model, revision=..., metadata_only=self.load_format == "dummy")`. A bare HF ID gets loader allow_patterns and LoadConfig.ignore_patterns `["original/**/*"]` (config/load.py:102).

</details>

🔴 Prefixed models whose config `auto_map` points at another repo ("repo--Class") now fail to start even without `trust_remote_code`, though a bare ID still loads natively. resolve_model_source always downloads every cross-repo code reference and never sees `trust_remote_code`. A missing, gated or offline-uncached code repo therefore aborts startup. Fix: pass `trust_remote_code` from EngineArgs to the model, tokenizer and draft calls, and leave `auto_map` untouched when it is False. That matches the PR's claim to respect it. Transformers' `custom_object_save` writes such references into many fine-tunes (Phi-3, InternLM, DeepSeek). Those HF repo IDs often do not exist on ModelScope.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `vllm serve modelscope://org/phi3-finetune` (or `hf://...`) without --trust-remote-code. The repo's config.json `auto_map` holds a cross-repo reference such as "microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct--configuration_phi3.Phi3Config". create_model_config (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:943) calls resolve_model_source. Its local_reference (vllm/model_hub.py:76-89) splits on "--" and calls download(code_repo, ...) unconditionally. On ModelScope that HF repo ID often does not exist, and under HF_HUB_OFFLINE the code repo may not be cached. The exception is re-raised with a note (model_hub.py:69-71), and engine startup fails. On the base branch the same model, given as a bare ID with or without VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE, loads natively: with trust_remote_code False, auto_map is never consulted. resolve_model_source has no trust_remote_code parameter, and none of the three call sites (arg_utils.py:943, :957, :2168) passes one, so nothing gates this path.

**Verification:** `resolve_model_source` in vllm/model_hub.py takes no trust_remote_code parameter. For any auto_map value containing "--", `local_reference` downloads the code repo with no condition, so a failed fetch aborts EngineArgs.create_model_config. On the base branch, vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:411-415 uses the native class and ignores `auto_map`.

</details>

🔴 With the Rust frontend enabled, `vllm serve hf://owner/model` (or `modelscope://`) loads the engine and then fails at frontend startup. The served name also comes out as `hf://owner/model`. Only the Python frontends were updated: `RustFrontendProcessManager` (vllm/v1/utils.py:352) still forwards the raw CLI `model_tag` and `tokenizer`. Fix: give the Rust frontend the values `EngineArgs.__post_init__` resolved, so `model_tag`/`tokenizer` are the local paths from `vllm_config.model_config`. Its default served name should also be the bare repo ID, matching the Python app_state paths.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve hf://owner/model`, or the same with `modelscope://` or `--tokenizer hf://...`, which goes through run_multi_api_server in vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py:353. The prefix is resolved only on the EngineArgs copy (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:943-961). The CLI Namespace `args` keeps the prefixed string, and RustFrontendProcessManager serializes it as `model_tag` (vllm/v1/utils.py:352-354). The Rust frontend reads `model_tag` as `ModelArgs.id` (rust/src/cmd/src/cli/model.rs:19). `SourceFiles::open` (rust/src/text/src/backend/hf/model_files.rs:223-256) finds no such directory, treats `hf://owner/model` as an HF repo and fails with "failed to fetch model 'hf://owner/model'". It never contacts ModelScope for `modelscope://`. `effective_served_model_names` (rust/src/server/src/lib.rs:71) would also publish `hf://owner/model`, while the engine metrics use `owner/model`. The PR's strip_model_source fix in both Python app_state files does not reach this path. The feature is documented for `vllm serve` but does not work on the Rust frontend.

**Verification:** The prefix is resolved only on the EngineArgs object. The argparse Namespace `args` is never changed. `SourceFiles::open` (rust/src/text/src/backend/hf/model_files.rs:221-256) checks `Path::new(model_id).is_dir()`. So the engine finishes loading from the resolved snapshot, and then the frontend fails to start.

</details>

🔴 Ray multi-node deployments without a shared cache now fail to load prefixed models. Workers on other nodes get a head-node-only path instead of a repo ID. `__post_init__` replaces `self.model` with the head's local snapshot or `hub_sources` overlay path, and `create_speculative_config` (2168) does the same for the draft. Fix: keep the original Hub reference available to workers, for example in `model_weights` as runai does, so each node resolves its own copy. Otherwise, reject or document cross-node use. Bare IDs keep working because every worker downloads them itself.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger condition: `--distributed-executor-backend ray` with TP/PP workers on other nodes, where the HF cache or download_dir and VLLM_CACHE_ROOT are not on a shared filesystem. docs/serving/parallelism_scaling.md:222 explicitly supports this setup for repo IDs ("Otherwise, supply a Hugging Face token"). EngineArgs.__post_init__ (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:943) sets `self.model` to a path such as `.../models--o--m/snapshots/<sha>` or `<VLLM_CACHE_ROOT>/hub_sources/<digest>/m`, created only on the head node. The draft gets the same treatment at arg_utils.py:2168. vllm_config goes to the Ray workers as-is (vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py:393). On a remote node, DefaultModelLoader sees `os.path.isdir` is false (default_loader.py:163) and calls download_weights_from_hf with that absolute path. validate_repo_id rejects it, and startup fails. On base, a bare `owner/model` stays a repo ID, so each worker downloads its own weights. No `model_weights` fallback is set, so the original `hf://`/`modelscope://` reference is lost.

**Verification:** In `EngineArgs.__post_init__` (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py ~943), `resolve_model_source` (vllm/model_hub.py:73) returns a head-node path for prefixed models, and `create_speculative_config` does the same for the draft. On a remote node, `is_local = os.path.isdir(model_name_or_path)` (default_loader.py:163) is False, so the worker crashes during model load. Bare IDs do not regress.

</details>

🔴 Users who pass `--code-revision` for the model and a separate prefixed tokenizer (`--tokenizer hf://other/tok`) with custom-code `auto_map` can now fail at startup. The `resolve_source` partial binds the model's `self.code_revision` and is reused for a tokenizer from another repo at arg_utils.py:957. In `local_reference`, a bare `auto_map` entry plus a non-None `code_revision` triggers a download of the tokenizer repo at the model's code revision. Fix: give the tokenizer `code_revision` only when the tokenizer is the model (same string), as `tokenizer_args_from_config` does; otherwise pass `code_revision=None`.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is `--model hf://a/model --code-revision X --tokenizer hf://b/tok`, or a bare model with a prefixed tokenizer, where b/tok's tokenizer_config.json has a bare auto_map such as `"AutoTokenizer": ["tokenization_b.Tok", null]`. arg_utils.py:934-939 binds `code_revision=self.code_revision` into `resolve_source`, and that partial resolves the tokenizer at arg_utils.py:957-961. In vllm/model_hub.py `local_reference`, a value with no `--` and a non-None `code_revision` becomes `code_repo = repo_id` (the tokenizer repo) and calls `download(code_repo, code_revision, code_only=True)`. The model's revision X usually does not exist in repo b/tok, so snapshot_download raises and EngineArgs.__post_init__ fails. When the download does succeed, the tokenizer code is silently pinned to the wrong revision. On the base branch, vllm/tokenizers/registry.py:191-194 applies `code_revision` to the tokenizer only when `config.tokenizer == config.model`, so a separate tokenizer repo never sees the model's code revision.

**Verification:** normal (narrow trigger). The condition: `--code-revision X` is set and `--tokenizer` is a prefixed reference to a different repo (e.g. `hf://b/tok`) whose `*config*.json` has a bare `auto_map` entry, and X is not a valid revision in b/tok (for example, a commit hash from the model repo).

Mechanism, verified:
- arg_utils.py:934-939 builds `resolve_source = functools.partial(resolve_model_source, ..., code_revision=self.code_revision)`.

</details>

The prefix is stripped from the default served name only in the two app_state launchers. The snapshot manifest still builds its name from the raw `hf://`/`modelscope://` string via `get_served_model_name` (vllm/snapshot/runtime.py:869). Fix: work out the default served name in one place, e.g. have `get_served_model_name` call `strip_model_source`, so the server and the manifest always agree.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `vllm snapshot create hf://owner/model --revision <40-hex sha>` with no --served-model-name. validate_create_args accepts this because Path("hf://owner/model") does not exist. LocalSnapshotTools.make_manifest (vllm/snapshot/runtime.py:866-879) stores served_model_name=get_served_model_name("hf://owner/model", None), which is "hf://owner/model". The restored child serves HTTP through build_and_serve and init_app_state, which registers BaseModelPath name "owner/model" (api_server/app_state.py:53). restore_snapshot then calls request_oracle (runtime.py:1229) with model "hf://owner/model". OpenAIModelRegistry.check_model returns 404 "The model `hf://owner/model` does not exist.", urlopen raises HTTPError, and restore_snapshot cleans up and fails every time. On the base branch a prefixed model never loads, so create fails early instead of producing an artifact that cannot be restored. The strip_model_source calls added to both app_state launchers do not cover this path because the manifest computes the name on its own.

**Verification:** With no --served-model-name, `get_served_model_name` (vllm/config/model.py:2331-2342) returns `model` unchanged, so the manifest stores "hf://owner/model". `init_app_state` now registers `served_model_names = [strip_model_source(args.model)]` (app_state.py:53). The create-side canary does not catch this: it runs on the engine directly, not over HTTP.

</details>

Line 948 stores the prefixed URI in `model_weights`. maybe_override_with_speculators (arg_utils.py:2316) then swaps `self.model` to the verifier but keeps the stale `model_weights`. 🟡 (optional) Prefixed `hf://` models are no longer pinned to one commit. If the branch moves during startup or before a worker (re)loads, config and weights can come from different commits. Resolution runs in EngineArgs with `revision=None`, and ModelConfig.resolve_revision then skips the local snapshot path. Each later `snapshot_download` call resolves `main` again: BaseModelLoader.load_model, every TP worker, and every pattern in download_model_weights. Fix: resolve the requested revision to a commit hash once, before the first download. Store it in `revision`, and in the draft revision too, so every later call uses that commit.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

On base, ModelConfig.__post_init__ (vllm/config/model.py:643) calls resolve_revision for a bare HF ID, turning a branch into a commit hash. Its docstring says this "avoids races if the branch moves while the model is loading" (repo_utils.py:84). With `hf://owner/model`, EngineArgs.__post_init__ (arg_utils.py:943-947) passes `self.revision` (often None) to resolve_model_source. It then sets `self.model` to the snapshot dir, and resolve_revision returns early because `Path(repo_id).exists()` (repo_utils.py:100), so `model_config.revision` stays None. On every worker, base_loader.py:56-58 calls resolve_model_source with revision=None, and DefaultModelLoader passes `revision=revision` (None) to download_model_weights. That makes 1+N separate snapshot_download calls, each resolving `main` again. A push to the repo between config fetch and load, between TP ranks, or before a later worker start or `reload_weights` mixes commits: config from A with weights from B, or different shards on different ranks. The same applies to prefixed drafts (speculative.py:1387-1415).

**Verification:** The trigger is a moving branch: an `hf://owner/model` source is loaded with no revision, or with a branch name, and the Hub branch gets a new commit between EngineArgs resolution and weight loading. The revision stays None or a branch name (repo_utils.py:100). On base, a bare HF ID is pinned to a commit hash at this point.

</details>

## Overview

Some deployments use a main model from ModelScope and a draft model from Hugging Face. The global `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` switch cannot express this combination. This PR adds explicit, per-model Hub selection.

For example, use [GLM-4.7-Flash from ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-4.7-Flash) with [thoughtworks/GLM-4.7-Flash-Eagle3 from Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/thoughtworks/GLM-4.7-Flash-Eagle3). I could not find a same-ID ModelScope mirror of this draft.

```bash
vllm serve modelscope://ZhipuAI/GLM-4.7-Flash \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"hf://thoughtworks/GLM-4.7-Flash-Eagle3","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

## Claims

- Support `hf://owner/model` and `modelscope://owner/model` for the model, tokenizer, and speculative draft model.
- Explicit prefixes override the global Hub setting; bare `owner/model` IDs and local paths retain their existing behavior.
- Resolve explicit sources into local SDK snapshots before normal loading, reusing authentication and caching without cross-Hub fallback.
- Keep ModelScope optional and the shared helper under `transformers_utils`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_model_hub.py \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py -q --tb=short
# 47 passed

VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_model_hub.py \
  -k 'hf_downloader_survives or mixed_sources' -q --tb=short
# 5 passed
```

Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed. A GPU integration test is included but has not been run locally; model evaluation is pending.

## Details

The initial scope is single-node Python execution with `auto`, `hf`, `safetensors`, or `pt` loaders. Explicit model sources download repository snapshots, potentially including multiple weight formats; tokenizer-only sources download metadata without weights.

Cross-repository `auto_map`, separate code revisions, and automatic speculator target inference are outside this initial scope. Unsupported cases fail explicitly and can use pre-downloaded local paths instead. This revision removes the earlier loader-specific changes.

Prior open-PR searches found no direct match for per-model HF/ModelScope selection. AI assistance was used.

🔴 Users who add an `hf://` or `modelscope://` prefix now download the whole repo, including weights vLLM never loads. A bare ID only fetches what the loader selects. Unless load_format is dummy, `ignore_patterns` is None, so the snapshot pulls every file. That includes `original/` .pth checkpoints, duplicate .bin/.safetensors copies and every GGUF quant. The metadata-only deny-list at :51 also misses *.h5, *.msgpack and *.onnx. Fix: build an allow-list from the loader's rules for the load format, and apply LoadConfig `ignore_patterns` (default `original/**/*`). For tokenizer and dummy downloads, allow only config, tokenizer and code files.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `vllm serve hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` or `modelscope://...`, which reaches resolve_model_source via EngineArgs.create_model_config (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:943). There, metadata_only is False, so `ignore_patterns` is None (vllm/model_hub.py:50-54), and snapshot_download fetches every file in the repo. On the base branch, DefaultModelLoader downloads only allow_patterns such as ["*.safetensors"] (default_loader.py:186-201). It also honors LoadConfig.ignore_patterns, which defaults to ["original/**/*"] (vllm/config/load.py:102). For Llama-3 repos that adds a second full consolidated .pth copy. For GGUF repos it adds every quantization, and repos that keep both .bin and .safetensors double the download. The local-path loader skips its own filtering download, so nothing removes this cost. `self.ignore_patterns` (arg_utils.py:712) is never passed to resolve_model_source. The tokenizer download (arg_utils.py:960) and the dummy download still pull TF/Flax/ONNX weights (*.h5, *.msgpack, *.onnx), because the deny-list at model_hub.py:51 does not cover them.

**Verification:** vllm/model_hub.py:47-55 sets `"ignore_patterns": ([...] if metadata_only else None)` and passes no allow_patterns, so every file in the repo is downloaded. EngineArgs.create_model_config calls `resolve_source(model, revision=..., metadata_only=self.load_format == "dummy")`. A bare HF ID gets loader allow_patterns and LoadConfig.ignore_patterns `["original/**/*"]` (config/load.py:102).

</details>

🔴 Prefixed models whose config `auto_map` points at another repo ("repo--Class") now fail to start even without `trust_remote_code`, though a bare ID still loads natively. resolve_model_source always downloads every cross-repo code reference and never sees `trust_remote_code`. A missing, gated or offline-uncached code repo therefore aborts startup. Fix: pass `trust_remote_code` from EngineArgs to the model, tokenizer and draft calls, and leave `auto_map` untouched when it is False. That matches the PR's claim to respect it. Transformers' `custom_object_save` writes such references into many fine-tunes (Phi-3, InternLM, DeepSeek). Those HF repo IDs often do not exist on ModelScope.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `vllm serve modelscope://org/phi3-finetune` (or `hf://...`) without --trust-remote-code. The repo's config.json `auto_map` holds a cross-repo reference such as "microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct--configuration_phi3.Phi3Config". create_model_config (vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:943) calls resolve_model_source. Its local_reference (vllm/model_hub.py:76-89) splits on "--" and calls download(code_repo, ...) unconditionally. On ModelScope that HF repo ID often does not exist, and under HF_HUB_OFFLINE the code repo may not be cached. The exception is re-raised with a note (model_hub.py:69-71), and engine startup fails. On the base branch the same model, given as a bare ID with or without VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE, loads natively: with trust_remote_code False, auto_map is never consulted. resolve_model_source has no trust_remote_code parameter, and none of the three call sites (arg_utils.py:943, :957, :2168) passes one, so nothing gates this path.

**Verification:** `resolve_model_source` in vllm/model_hub.py takes no trust_remote_code parameter. For any auto_map value containing "--", `local_reference` downloads the code repo with no condition, so a failed fetch aborts EngineArgs.create_model_config. On the base branch, vllm/transformers_utils/config.py:411-415 uses the native class and ignores `auto_map`.

</details>
